facts.rationale: Corrects the unsupported claim that source declaration order proves a consecutive 64-byte compiled data section.
facts.value: The canonical source declares two private arrays of type static u32[8]: SectorSizeTable = {8192, 16384, 32768, 65536, 131072, 262144, 0, 0}, followed in declaration order by LatencyTable = {4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512}. These declarations establish source types and values, not compiled section placement, adjacency or total section size.

evidence.why: Probe returns the table entry without geometry rejection.
Division precedes the zero-sector and minimum-block guard.

facts.rationale: Preserves the useful lookup flow while correcting the omitted evaluation order and distinguishing probe classification from mount geometry checking.
facts.value: Device-ID bits 11–13 index SectorSizeTable: CARDProbeEx reports the selected byte count, while DoMount stores it in sectorSize and uses it to calculate cBlock. Bits 8–10 index LatencyTable for card->latency. DoMount computes cBlock by dividing by sectorSize before testing sectorSize == 0 or cBlock < 8 and assigning -2 on that branch. Consequently, the later guard must not be described as safely rejecting zero-sized entries before division; CARDProbeEx itself can report a zero table entry with READY.

evidence.why: Signature, explicit suppression return and missing normal-path return.
Canonical caller consumes probe results for change detection.

facts.rationale: Separates exact signature and caller intent from an unsupported guarantee about the normal-path return value; compiled behavior remains unverified.
facts.value: Declared as int CARDProbe(long chan), with chan passed to the EXI/card probe. The GameChoice & 0x80 branch explicitly returns zero. The normal path calls EXIProbe(chan) and reaches the end without an explicit return, so this C body alone does not establish a defined returned probe value on that path. Snapshot polling nevertheless stores and compares CARDProbe results, demonstrating the intended presence-query interface.
